text:
ela: Quick sync — we need to lock down the routing decision contract that the console and telemetry will display. Do we expose the full decision chain or a compact header + sampled full traces?

mike: full chain is great for debugging, but worried about payload size and PII. :thinking:

sasha: Agree with mike. My suggestion: compact headers for every request, and sampled full decision traces (e.g., 0.5%-1%). Compact should include final variant + routing reason + tier + region.

jorge: Can we agree on a compact header shape? Proposal:
```
X-Redwood-Routing: tier=enterprise;region=eu;variant=v2-q4;reason=latency_priority;trace_id=abc123
X-Redwood-Routing-Flags: cached=true;prefix_hits=3;batching=auto
```
compact values are semicolon-delimited, URL-safe. trace_id maps to sampled full trace when available.

tina: UX ask: traces we show should be deterministic for a given customer so we can correlate incidents. Sampling by request rng is noisy. Use deterministic hash on account_id -> sample bucket.

anil: Important: we can never store raw prompts in full traces for EU customers. Either strip prompt text or store only a stable hash. Must check GDPR retention.

mike: For quotas/billing insights, we should also surface a lightweight route_cost_estimate header so console can break down cost by routing decision. e.g. `route_cost_est=0.0025` (USD).

ela: Good call. To summarize my rough contract idea:
- Every request gets compact headers (tier, region, final_variant, reason, flags, route_cost_est, trace_id if sampled)
- Full decision traces stored only for sampled requests (deterministic sampling by account_id)
- Full traces redact prompt text, keep hashed prompt id + model KV + kernel path details + timestamps
- Retention: 30d for full traces, 365d for compact metadata
- Customer opt-out to disable storing full traces (still route normally)

jorge: Small note re: trace size: we should cap kernel path details to first N steps (N=50?) and aggregate repeated policy checks into counts to avoid huge payloads.

sasha: Also expose a rollout tag on header so console shows canary percentage + rollout id. e.g. `rollout=canary-2026-03:v0.1:10%`

deploy-bot: Canary rollout `canary-2026-03` -> eu region -> 10% traffic applied.

tina: UX: console needs an affordance to fetch full trace on demand when available (link from compact entry -> full trace viewer). If trace missing due to sampling, show explanation and "request trace not sampled" CTA.

anil: Security question: who can view full traces? Need RBAC — only SRE + customer owner + support with memo. We should audit views.

mike: We should version this contract. v1=compact+sampled-full. If we change fields later, bump header namespace `X-Redwood-Routing-v2` or include `contract=v1` field.

ela: Action items:
- eng-platform: define exact compact header names + enum values (owner: jorge) -> due EOD Fri
- eng-runtime: implement deterministic sampling + redaction (owner: anil) -> spike next week
- devex/UI: sketch trace viewer with link to compact entries + opt-out UI (owner: tina) -> mock by Tue
- legal/privacy: confirm retention + EU redaction approach (owner: sasha) -> sync w/ privacy 

jorge: I'll draft a small spec with header names and a tiny example payload. Posting here when ready.

ela: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD I'll fold these into the UX ticket. :+1:
